title: Define hybrid admission contract and deprecation path for community open-model entries
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Background: We continue to onboard community-supplied open models into the Redwood model catalog. Recent incidents and runtime incompatibilities exposed a gap between the lightweight intake flow and long-term maintenance expectations (version pinning, compatibility notes, deprecation signals). This ticket clarifies a hybrid admission contract that balances fast ingestion for experimentation with enforced governance for models that move to production-facing channels.

Goals:
- Define a clear admission contract for community models that distinguishes Experimental, Support-Limited, and Production-Eligible states.
- Specify required metadata, runtime compatibility signals, and automatic vs. manual pinning triggers for each state.
- Create an explicit deprecation path with notification windows, automated fallback behavior in the runtime, and rollback criteria.
- Produce acceptance criteria, a short PRD to sync infra/eng/design, and a checklist for solutions/SEs when recommending a model to customers.

Problem statement: Currently, models can be ingested rapidly, but the catalog lacks consistent pinning semantics and clear deprecation flow. This leads to: intermittent regressions in latency/accuracy when newer community variants are served; ambiguity for Dedicated/Private customers about supported versions; and manual, error-prone rollback processes.

Scope (this ticket):
- Define the hybrid admission contract document (states + required fields + transitions).
- Enumerate compatibility signals the runtime must emit for each uploaded model (kernel suitability, quantization safe flags, perf profile, max context length tested).
- Define automated pinning rules (soft pin, hard pin) and criteria that trigger manual review.
- Draft deprecation timeline templates and runtime fallback behavior (model variant fallback order, logging/events).
- Deliver acceptance criteria, a one-page PRD, and a checklist artifact for Catalog intake.

Out of scope: full infra implementation, UI changes in Console (will be follow-up tickets), detailed KMS/security controls for private customers (handled by ENG security team separately).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Admission contract doc created and approved by PM, Runtime, and Catalog owners: document must list Experimental / Support-Limited / Production-Eligible states and show allowed transitions.
2) For each state, required metadata fields are defined and validated in the intake flow: provenance, model-weights-hash, recommended quantization profile, minimal perf profile (p50 latency, throughput estimate), and tested context length.
3) Compatibility signals: at least five runtime signals enumerated (kernel_family, quantization_safe, kv_cache_behavior, max_sequence_validated, failing_ops_list) and example payloads provided.
4) Pinning rules: specify "soft pin" (auto-rollback window + advisory) and "hard pin" (manual approval required). Provide decision matrix and at least 3 example scenarios.
5) Deprecation policy: 30/14/7 notification windows defined and automated runtime fallback order for at least two families of compatible variants with clear logging events documented.
6) Checklist artifact for Solutions/SE: 10-step checklist published in Confluence with links to runtime docs and sample API calls for pin/unpin.
7) Stakeholders sign-off: PM (Priya), Runtime Eng lead (Sofia Alvarez), Catalog owner (Liam O'Connor), and Security reviewer (Aisha Patel) sign off in comments.
8) Backwards-compatible runtime changes required are scoped and owned (list of ENG tickets created or referenced).
tasks: Write hybrid admission contract draft (PM + Runtime)
Collect runtime compatibility signals and example payloads (Runtime Eng)
Draft pinning decision matrix and scenario examples
Define deprecation notification windows and fallback behavior
Create Confluence intake checklist and link templates
Run 1 internal intake exercise using a low-risk community model to validate flow
Circulate for stakeholder review and collect sign-offs
Create follow-up ENG tickets for implementation (pin enforcement, telemetry events, automated notifications)
risks: Insufficient runtime telemetry to determine safe fallback behavior
Ambiguous compatibility signals leading to incorrect pin decisions
Operational load from manual review queues if soft pin thresholds poorly tuned
Confusion for Dedicated/Private customers if pin semantics are not communicated clearly
